s.t:
Install, maintain, and repair telemetry systems and recording and metering devices.
Support safe operation of hydroelectric units, performing startup/shutdown, synchronization, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), clearances, and routine/emergency switching at system voltages.
Install, test, and maintain protective relays, control circuits, excitation systems, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) interfaces, and interpret drawings and logic diagrams.
Maintain motors, Motor Control Centers (MCCs), battery systems, grounding grids, lighting circuits, HVAC electrical systems, and perform preventive maintenance on auxiliary systems.
Follow Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), National Fire Protection Association’s (NFPA) 70E/dam safety rules; perform arc-flash assessments, hazard analyses, emergency response, and complete accurate documentation and reports.
EXPERIENCE: A specific length of training and experience is not required, but you must show evidence of training or experience of sufficient scope and quality of your ability to do the work of this position.

Evidence which demonstrates you possess the knowledge, skills, and ability to perform the duties of this position must be supported by detailed descriptions of such on your resume. Applicants will be rated in accordance with the OPM Qualification Standard Handbook Federal Wage System Qualifications.

SCREEN-OUT ELEMENT: Your qualifications will first be evaluated against the prescribed screen out element. Those applicants who appear to possess at least the minimal acceptable qualification requirement are considered for further rating; those who do not are rated ineligible and are eliminated.

Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below: 1. Ability to do the work of the position without more than normal supervision. (SCREEN OUT) (OPM Job Element 1) 2. Knowledge of Electrical Equipment (OPM Job Element 2B) 3.

Theory of Instruments (electrical, electronic) used in Shop and Trade Practices (OPM Job Element 25-D) 4. Ability to Use and Maintain Hand tools (OPM Job Element 81-B) 5. Troubleshooting (Electrical) (OPM Job Element 96A) 6.

Ability to Use Electrical Drawings (OPM Job Element 75J) If your knowledge and ability in the SCREEN OUT factor above is not sufficient, you will receive no further consideration.

In preparing your application, describe in detail the experience and training which you have had that specifically prepared you for this job and to perform the duties described for this job. Experience should be clearly described and documented in your resume.

The qualifications reviewer will not assume performance of such duties by Job Titles alone. Address your knowledge, skills and/or abilities in the areas shown in the job related factors. Minimum qualifications for trades and labor positions are determined by evaluation of job elements.

You must meet at least 2 points on the screen-out element(s) and obtain an average of at least 2 points on all of the job elements in order to be considered qualified for this position.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Physical Efforts and Working Conditions: Work requires heavy physical exertion.

The work involves unassisted lifting and carrying of items weighing over forty-five pounds or up to fifty pounds (i.e., tools and equipment components); pulling and pushing of two- and four-wheel carts loaded with tools and equipment weighing up to two hundred pounds; prolonged standing; recurring climbing flights of stairs; and climbing and working on ladders and scaffolding up to 254 feet.

Duties also involve operating a pick-up truck, one-ton truck, and a 24,000-pound GVW bucket truck. The position requires sufficient hearing acuity to discern equipment noises and normal visual acuity to read diagrams, technical documents, and manuals.

Work is performed in physically tight spaces requiring prolonged kneeling and squatting; below ground in dam corridors to depths of up to 263 feet; on high structures including cranes on the dam up to 254 feet; and above water at the dam intake and the powerhouse transformer deck.

Works indoors and outdoors in all types of weather conditions and temperature extremes. Exposed to high and constant noise levels from diesel generators, sandblasting equipment, hydroelectric turbines, and generators.

Exposed to heat, extensive dust from sandblasting, contaminated air from diesel exhaust and welding fumes, and dangerous chemicals such as alcohol, battery acid, and cleaning solvents.

Subject to electrical burns and shock from generating and electrical distribution equipment; and to falls from slippery, wet, and uneven walking surfaces at the dam penstocks and valves.

Exposed to eye hazards from dust, welding, and grinding particles; and to injury from machinery with dangerous moving parts including drills, saws, various machine shop equipment, and machinery in motion very close to the incumbent such as motor shafts, pumps, and compressors.

Requires the use of protective devices such as ear plugs, safety hats, non-conductive gloves and footwear, and similar protective gear. The occasional use of a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) or face-fitted respirator may be required following a medical examination to determine any limitations.

Work may occur below ground in dam corridors to depths of fifty feet, on high structures including cranes on the dam (up to 254 feet), and above water at the dam intake and the powerhouse transformer deck.

All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description.

Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions.

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must meet any screen-out element listed, and show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on the quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Working Conditions: The work is performed both inside and outside.

Electrical workers are sometimes required to make repairs and installations in bad weather; in work areas that are noisy, dirty, dusty, and greasy; on scaffolding or cranes at heights of 9 meters (30 feet) or more; and in close quarters such as manholes, or attics.

They are occasionally exposed to the possibility of injury from falling, electrical shock, burns, and rotary devices such as electrical motors. They are frequently exposed to the possibility of cuts and bruises.

They are exposed to danger from explosions of equipment and cables in manholes and vaults, as well as danger from high voltage electrical shock, burns from solder, broken bones, cuts, and bruises.

They are exposed to heat and noise when working in substations or power-generating facilities, to extremes of weather when working outdoors, and to unpleasant odors and wet slippery surfaces when working in manholes.

They are subject to electrical burns while working around high voltage electrical lines, broken bones from falls from poles, and strains from awkward work positions. They are exposed to chemicals such as insulation oil from transformers and oil switches.

They use protective devices such as earplugs, safety hats, and nonconductive gloves and footwear.

Physical Effort: Workers frequently perform moderately heavy lifting, pulling, and carrying of equipment and material weighing up to 18 kilograms (40 pounds) and occasionally, they lift or pull heavy cables and equipment weighing more than 23 kilograms (50 pounds) with the help of weight handling equipment or with assistance from other workers.

They use block and tackle, pulleys, or other lifting devices. They crouch, stand, kneel, and stoop while installing, repairing, or testing electrical equipment in confined spaces such as enclosed switch gear, or in structures such as overhead bus and conduit assemblies.

Workers work above ground from aerial bucket trucks and poles, at ground level, and in trenches, or manholes. Work requires bending, stooping, climbing, and standing for long periods while installing, repairing, and testing electrical equipment in manholes and on overhead distribution lines in tiring and uncomfortable positions.

Electrical workers make repairs and installations from ladders, scaffolding, platforms, and other hard-to-reach places.

· Planifier son propre travail : ordre des étapes, durées, coordination avec les autres corps de métier et avec le chef de projet.
· Organiser les moyens nécessaires : accès, échafaudage, nacelle, coupures, autorisations d'accès.
· Encadrer ponctuellement un apprenti ou un monteur sur la partie AC.
· Tenir le rapport journalier, les heures et les photos d'avancement.
· Signaler immédiatement tout écart de délai, de coût ou de faisabilité - le plus tôt possible.
2.3 Mesures, sécurité et documents
Sans documents, le chantier n'est pas fini.
· Contrôle propre de l'installation selon la NIBT et l'OIBT.
· Protocoles de mesure complets : continuité du conducteur de protection, résistance d'isolement, impédance de boucle, courant de court-circuit, contrôle des DDR, ordre des phases, mesure de terre.
· Établissement du rapport de sécurité et des annexes, dans les délais et sans reprise.
· Respect des règles de sécurité au travail : cinq règles de sécurité, consignation, EPI, travail sous tension interdit sauf procédure.
· Signalement des non-conformités constatées sur les installations existantes rencontrées.

s.h: 3. PARTIE DC, MISE EN SERVICE ET MONITORING - SOUHAITÉE
s.t:
Souhaitée à l'entrée, indispensable à terme. Si elle n'est pas acquise, elle se forme chez nous - voir chapitre 6.
3.1 Côté DC
· Câblage des strings, connectique, coffrets DC, sectionneurs, parafoudres, cheminements et fixations.
· Contrôle des strings avant mise sous tension : polarité, tension à vide, résistance d'isolement, courant de court-circuit.
· Mesure de courbe I-V et interprétation ; recherche de défaut de string, de défaut d'isolement et d'arc.
· Thermographie de contrôle et lecture des résultats.
3.2 Mise en service des onduleurs
· Mise en service et paramétrage des onduleurs string et centraux : réglages réseau, courbes de puissance, limitation d'injection, protection de découplage.
· Paramétrage conforme aux exigences du GRD et aux prescriptions de raccordement en vigueur.
· Rédaction du protocole de mise en service et du relevé des paramètres appliqués.
· Diagnostic et traitement des défauts d'onduleur, échange sous garantie, relation avec le support fabricant.
3.3 Monitoring et informatique
· Installation et configuration du monitoring : passerelles, compteurs, capteurs, bus de communication (Modbus RTU/TCP, RS485), sondes d'irradiation et de température.
· Mise en réseau : adressage IP, VLAN, routeur 4G, VPN, ports, pare-feu côté client - savoir dialoguer avec un service informatique.
· Contrôle de la remontée des données, alarmes et seuils, création des accès client.
· Analyse d'un écart de production : distinguer un défaut d'installation, un défaut de matériel, un ombrage et une erreur de paramétrage.

s.h: 4. GROSSE PUISSANCE, BORNES ET BATTERIES - ATOUTS
s.t:
Non exigés à l'entrée, mais ce sont les domaines en croissance chez GTS. Une expérience dans l'un d'eux est un vrai plus.
Installations 500 kVA
· Tableaux de puissance, jeux de barres, câbles de forte section, raccordements sur transformateur.
· Sélectivité, coordination des protections, protection de découplage, contrôle de la qualité de réseau.
· Coordination avec le GRD sur les conditions de raccordement et les essais de conformité.
Bornes de recharge
· Installation, raccordement et mise en service de bornes AC et DC.
· Gestion dynamique de charge, délestage, comptage, communication et supervision (OCPP).
· Coordination avec la puissance disponible du bâtiment et l'autoconsommation PV.
Stockage batterie
· Installation, raccordement et mise en service de systèmes de stockage.
· Paramétrage des modes de fonctionnement : autoconsommation, écrêtage, alimentation de secours.
· Exigences de sécurité et de protection incendie applicables aux locaux de batteries.
Large autonomie sur le terrain, cadre clair sur ce qui engage l'entreprise.

· L'organisation de son chantier AC et l'ordre des étapes.
· Les choix de mise en œuvre, dans le respect des plans, de la NIBT et des règles de l'art.
· La liste de matériel et les besoins en moyens de chantier, transmis pour commande.
· L'arrêt d'une opération si les conditions de sécurité ne sont pas réunies - sans discussion ni justification ultérieure.

s.t:

En tant qu'Aide Électricien(ne), vos principales missions incluront :
* Assister les électriciens dans l'installation, la maintenance et la réparation des systèmes électriques.
* Préparer et organiser le matériel nécessaire pour les interventions.
* Effectuer des tâches de câblage et de raccordement sous supervision.
* Respecter les normes de sécurité et les procédures en vigueur.

Nous recherchons un(e) candidat(e) répondant aux critères suivants :
* Expérience préalable dans un poste similaire ou formation de base en électricité (un atout).

* Connaissance des outils
* Fiabilité, ponctualité et sens des responsabilités.
* Permis de conduire valable en Suisse (un plus).
